And their foolishness he accounted as a favor,
that is to say, because it alienated him from the favor of al-Ashraf.
And the lords of the fortress of 'Imadiyyah agreed beforehand to surrender it.
And because without the command and permission of al-Ashraf he was not able to take anything,
he sent to al-Ashraf
and demanded permission.
And al-Ashraf disputed and would not permit him,
until Badr al-Din gave him the fortress which is called al-Haditha, which is beside Nisibis, and the region of the Jazira (Between the Two Rivers).
And then Badr al-Din took 'Imadiyyah,
and he repaid great good things to those who surrendered it, more than what he had promised.
And the people of the other fortresses heard,
and they all surrendered.
And it was very marvelous,
that while a multitude of armies were gathered together from Syria, Mesopotamia, Armenia, and the rest of the places, they were not able to take these fortresses,
yet Badr al-Din by his cunning without violence gained dominion over them.
And that saying was fulfilled:
“It is better to trust in the Lord,
than to put confidence in princes.”
And in that same year died Malik al-Mansur Nasir al-Din Muhammad, son of Malik al-Muzaffar Taqi al-Din 'Umar, son of Shahanshah, son of Ayyub, lord of Hamath,
being fifty years of age.
And he commanded that his eldest son,
who was in Egypt with his maternal uncle Malik al-Kamil,
and whose name was Malik al-Muzaffar Taqi al-Din,
should succeed to his place.
The nobles sent and brought his other son from Damascus,
whose name was Malik al-Nasir Qilij Arslan,
and surrendered Hamath to him.
And in the year 618
618 of the Arabs [1221 AD],
Malik al-Mu'azzam, lord of Damascus, went,
and Malik al-Ashraf,
and the lord of Mardin,
and the army of Aleppo,
and Malik al-Nasir, lord of Hamath,
and Malik al-Mujahid, lord of Homs, to the aid of Malik al-Kamil.
And they all went together and encamped against Damietta,
and they pressed hard upon it and cut off the roads against the Franks.
And the Franks were afraid and agreed to surrender Damietta together with all the Arab prisoners who were in Acre,
and that the Arabs should allow them to go out and depart to their country in peace.
And al-Kamil took from them, the Franks, hostages with him,
until they should surrender Damietta and the prisoners.
